# durability - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/durability/^0.6/

## Expand description

`durability`: crash-consistent persistence primitives.

Scope:

- directory abstraction (`Directory`)
- on-disk framing constants (`formats`)
- append-only record log (`recordlog`)
- generic write-ahead log (`walog`)
- CRC-validated checkpoint snapshots (`checkpoint`)
- generic recovery (`recover::recover_with_wal`) and segment-specific recovery (`recover`,`publish`) with the default`postcard`feature

[§](https://docs.rs#features)Features

- `postcard`(default): serde/postcard typed WAL, checkpoint, recovery, and publish helpers.
- `async`: tokio-compatible async directory abstraction.
- `mmap`: mmap and advisory helpers.

With `default-features = false`, the crate still provides the directory abstraction,
raw record logs, raw checkpoint payloads, WAL framing/maintenance, and sync helpers.

[§](https://docs.rs#contract-what-you-can-rely-on)Contract (what you can rely on)

This crate is designed around two different “strength levels”:

- **Crash-consistent + integrity-checked**(default)- Detects corruption (CRC/magic/version/type mismatches) and errors loudly.
- Supports best-effort recovery of a **torn tail**(partial record write) in the**final**log segment.
- Guarantees a **prefix property**under best-effort replay: recovered operations are a prefix of the successfully written operation stream (no garbage / no reordering).

- **Stable-storage durability**(opt-in)- Requires explicit barriers (`fsync`/`sync_all`) and sometimes**parent directory sync**.
- Use `storage::sync_file``storage::sync_parent_dir``flush_and_sync()`helpers where you need “survives power loss after success” semantics.

- Requires explicit barriers (

Terminology:

- `flush()`is a- **visibility boundary**, not a stable-storage guarantee.
- “Best-effort” is intentionally narrow; it never masks corruption.

Note: this crate intentionally exposes *traits and framing*.
Higher-level crates generally decide directory layout, naming, and lifecycle policies,
but some primitives (notably `walog`) assume a conventional `wal/` directory.

## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

- `pub use error::`- [PersistenceError](https://docs.rs/error/enum.PersistenceError.html);
- `pub use error::`- [PersistenceResult](https://docs.rs/error/type.PersistenceResult.html);
- `pub use storage::`- [Directory](https://docs.rs/storage/trait.Directory.html);
- `pub use storage::`- [FsDirectory](https://docs.rs/storage/struct.FsDirectory.html);
- `pub use storage::`- [MemoryDirectory](https://docs.rs/storage/struct.MemoryDirectory.html);

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [async_](https://docs.rs/async_dir/index.html)- dir
- Async directory trait and blocking adapter.
- [checkpoint](https://docs.rs/checkpoint/index.html)
- Generic checkpoint file (single snapshot blob).
- [error](https://docs.rs/error/index.html)
- Error types for `durability`.
- [mmap](https://docs.rs/mmap/index.html)
- Memory-mapped file access with advisory hints.
- [publish](https://docs.rs/publish/index.html)
- Crash-safe checkpoint publishing and WAL truncation helpers.
- [recordlog](https://docs.rs/recordlog/index.html)
- Append-only record log (generic WAL primitive).
- [recover](https://docs.rs/recover/index.html)
- Crash recovery using checkpoint + WAL replay.
- [storage](https://docs.rs/storage/index.html)
- Storage abstraction for durability.
- [walog](https://docs.rs/walog/index.html)
- Write-ahead log (WAL) for incremental updates.

# postcard - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/postcard/^1.0/

## Expand description

[§](https://docs.rs#postcard)Postcard

Postcard is a `#![no_std]` focused serializer and deserializer for Serde.

Postcard aims to be convenient for developers in constrained environments, while allowing for flexibility to customize behavior as needed.

[§](https://docs.rs#design-goals)Design Goals

- Design primarily for `#![no_std]`usage, in embedded or other constrained contexts
- Support a maximal set of `serde`features, so`postcard`can be used as a drop in replacement
- Avoid special differences in code between communication code written for a microcontroller or a desktop/server PC
- Be resource efficient - memory usage, code size, developer time, and CPU time; in that order
- Allow library users to customize the serialization and deserialization behavior to fit their bespoke needs

[§](https://docs.rs#format-stability)Format Stability

As of v1.0.0, `postcard` has a documented and stable wire format. More information about this
wire format can be found in the `spec/` folder of the Postcard repository, or viewed online
at [https://postcard.jamesmunns.com](https://postcard.jamesmunns.com).

Work towards the Postcard Specification and portions of the Postcard 1.0 Release were sponsored by Mozilla Corporation.

[§](https://docs.rs#variable-length-data)Variable Length Data

All signed and unsigned integers larger than eight bits are encoded using a [Varint](https://postcard.jamesmunns.com/wire-format.html#varint-encoded-integers).
This includes the length of array slices, as well as the discriminant of `enums`.

For more information, see the [Varint](https://postcard.jamesmunns.com/wire-format.html#varint-encoded-integers) chapter of the wire specification.

[§](https://docs.rs#example---serializationdeserialization)Example - Serialization/Deserialization

Postcard can serialize and deserialize messages similar to other `serde` formats.

Using the default `heapless` feature to serialize to a `heapless::Vec<u8>`:

```
use core::ops::Deref;
use serde::{Serialize, Deserialize};
use postcard::{from_bytes, to_vec};
use heapless::Vec;
#[derive(Serialize, Deserialize, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
struct RefStruct<'a> {
    bytes: &'a [u8],
    str_s: &'a str,
}
let message = "hElLo";
let bytes = [0x01, 0x10, 0x02, 0x20];
let output: Vec<u8, 11> = to_vec(&RefStruct {
    bytes: &bytes,
    str_s: message,
}).unwrap();
assert_eq!(
    &[0x04, 0x01, 0x10, 0x02, 0x20, 0x05, b'h', b'E', b'l', b'L', b'o',],
    output.deref()
);
let out: RefStruct = from_bytes(output.deref()).unwrap();
assert_eq!(
    out,
    RefStruct {
        bytes: &bytes,
        str_s: message,
    }
);
```
Or the optional `alloc` feature to serialize to an `alloc::vec::Vec<u8>`:

```
use core::ops::Deref;
use serde::{Serialize, Deserialize};
use postcard::{from_bytes, to_allocvec};
extern crate alloc;
use alloc::vec::Vec;
#[derive(Serialize, Deserialize, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
struct RefStruct<'a> {
    bytes: &'a [u8],
    str_s: &'a str,
}
let message = "hElLo";
let bytes = [0x01, 0x10, 0x02, 0x20];
let output: Vec<u8> = to_allocvec(&RefStruct {
    bytes: &bytes,
    str_s: message,
}).unwrap();
assert_eq!(
    &[0x04, 0x01, 0x10, 0x02, 0x20, 0x05, b'h', b'E', b'l', b'L', b'o',],
    output.deref()
);
let out: RefStruct = from_bytes(output.deref()).unwrap();
assert_eq!(
    out,
    RefStruct {
        bytes: &bytes,
        str_s: message,
    }
);
```
[§](https://docs.rs#flavors)Flavors

`postcard` supports a system called `Flavors`, which are used to modify the way
postcard serializes or processes serialized data. These flavors act as “plugins” or “middlewares”
during the serialization or deserialization process, and can be combined to obtain complex protocol formats.

See the documentation of the `ser_flavors` or `de_flavors` modules for more information on usage.

[§](https://docs.rs#setup---cargotoml)Setup - `Cargo.toml`

Don’t forget to add [the  no-std subset](https://serde.rs/no-std.html) of

`serde` along with `postcard` to the `[dependencies]` section of your `Cargo.toml`!```
[dependencies]
postcard = "1.0.0"
# By default, `serde` has the `std` feature enabled, which makes it unsuitable for embedded targets
# disabling default-features fixes this
serde = { version = "1.0.*", default-features = false }
```

# sbits - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/sbits/^0.2/

## Expand description

[§](https://docs.rs#succinct-data-structures)Succinct Data Structures

*Near-optimal space with efficient queries.*

[§](https://docs.rs#intuition-first)Intuition First

Imagine a library where every book is stored in a tightly packed vacuum-sealed bag. It takes up the absolute minimum space (the information-theoretic limit). Usually, to find a specific page, you’d have to unseal the whole bag (decompress).

Succinct data structures allow you to “reach through” the vacuum seal and read specific pages, count words, or find the k-th occurrence of a character—all without unsealing the bag.

[§](https://docs.rs#the-problem)The Problem

Traditional data structures face a trade-off:

- **Pointers**: Fast queries ($O(1)$) but massive overhead ($O(n \log n)$ bits).
- **Compression**: Minimal space ($\log |C_n|$ bits) but no random access or queries ($O(n)$ to decompress).

[§](https://docs.rs#historical-context)Historical Context

```
1971  Fano        Fano's associative memory: early partitioning of bits
1974  Elias       Elias's static file storage: monotone sequences
1989  Jacobson    Defined the succinct paradigm in his PhD thesis (rank/select)
1996  Munro-Raman Constant-time rank and select in o(n) extra space
2003  Grossi      Wavelet trees for rank/select over arbitrary alphabets
2007  Ferragina   FM-index: compressed full-text search (the "BWT" era)
2022  Kurpicz     Modern engineering of rank9/select9 structures
```
Guy Jacobson’s key insight was that for many objects (like trees or bit vectors), we can build auxiliary structures that are much smaller than the data itself ($o(n)$ bits) but provide enough information to answer queries in constant time.

[§](https://docs.rs#mathematical-formulation)Mathematical Formulation

A data structure for a class of objects $C_n$ is:

- **Implicit**: Uses $\log |C_n| + O(1)$ bits.
- **Succinct**: Uses $\log |C_n| + o(\log |C_n|)$ bits.
- **Compact**: Uses $O(\log |C_n|)$ bits.

The fundamental operations are:

- `rank(i)`: The number of set bits (1s) in the range $[0, i]$.
- `select(k)`: The position of the $k$-th set bit.

[§](https://docs.rs#complexity-analysis)Complexity Analysis

- **Time**: $O(1)$ for rank/select in most modern implementations.
- **Space**: OPT + $o(n)$ bits (typically 5-20% overhead for auxiliary structures).

[§](https://docs.rs#what-could-go-wrong)What Could Go Wrong

- **Static vs Dynamic**: Most succinct structures are static. Inserting into a succinct bit vector usually requires rebuilding the auxiliary structures.
- **Cache Locality**: Constant time $O(1)$ doesn’t mean “fast” if it requires multiple random memory lookups for large bitsets.

[§](https://docs.rs#implementation-notes)Implementation Notes

This crate provides:

- `BitVector`
- `WaveletTree`
- `EliasFano`
- `PartitionedEliasFano`

[§](https://docs.rs#references)References

- Jacobson, G. (1989). “Succinct Static Data Structures.”
- Munro, J. I., & Raman, V. (1996). “Selection and counting on the fly.”
- Grossi, R., et al. (2003). “High-order entropy-compressed text indexes.”

## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

- `pub use bitvec::`- [BitVector](https://docs.rs/bitvec/struct.BitVector.html);
- `pub use elias_fano::`- [EliasFano](https://docs.rs/elias_fano/struct.EliasFano.html);
- `pub use error::`- [Error](https://docs.rs/error/enum.Error.html);
- `pub use partitioned_elias_fano::`- [PartitionedEliasFano](https://docs.rs/partitioned_elias_fano/struct.PartitionedEliasFano.html);
- `pub use wavelet::`- [WaveletTree](https://docs.rs/wavelet/struct.WaveletTree.html);

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [bitvec](https://docs.rs/bitvec/index.html)
- Cache-friendly succinct bit vector with rank/select support.
- [elias_](https://docs.rs/elias_fano/index.html)- fano
- Elias-Fano encoding for monotone sequences.
- [error](https://docs.rs/error/index.html)
- Error types and deserialization utilities for succinct data structures.
- [partitioned_](https://docs.rs/partitioned_elias_fano/index.html)- elias_ - fano
- Partitioned Elias–Fano for clustered monotone sequences.
- [wavelet](https://docs.rs/wavelet/index.html)
- Wavelet Matrix for arbitrary alphabets.

# thiserror - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/thiserror/^2.0/

## Expand description

This library provides a convenient derive macro for the standard library’s
[ std::error::Error](https://doc.rust-lang.org/core/error/trait.Error.html) trait.

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
use thiserror::Error;
#[derive(Error, Debug)]
pub enum DataStoreError {
    #[error("data store disconnected")]
    Disconnect(#[from] io::Error),
    #[error("the data for key `{0}` is not available")]
    Redaction(String),
    #[error("invalid header (expected {expected:?}, found {found:?})")]
    InvalidHeader {
        expected: String,
        found: String,
    },
    #[error("unknown data store error")]
    Unknown,
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#details)Details

-
Thiserror deliberately does not appear in your public API. You get the same thing as if you had written an implementation of `std::error::Error`
-
Errors may be enums, structs with named fields, tuple structs, or unit structs.
-
A `Display``#[error("...")]`messages on the struct or each variant of your enum, as shown above in the example.The messages support a shorthand for interpolating fields from the error. - `#[error("{var}")]`⟶- `write!("{}", self.var)`
- `#[error("{0}")]`⟶- `write!("{}", self.0)`
- `#[error("{var:?}")]`⟶- `write!("{:?}", self.var)`
- `#[error("{0:?}")]`⟶- `write!("{:?}", self.0)`
 These shorthands can be used together with any additional format args, which may be arbitrary expressions. For example: `#[derive(Error, Debug)] pub enum Error { #[error("invalid rdo_lookahead_frames {0} (expected < {max})", max = i32::MAX)] InvalidLookahead(u32), }`If one of the additional expression arguments needs to refer to a field of the struct or enum, then refer to named fields as `.var`and tuple fields as`.0`.`#[derive(Error, Debug)] pub enum Error { #[error("first letter must be lowercase but was {:?}", first_char(.0))] WrongCase(String), #[error("invalid index {idx}, expected at least {} and at most {}", .limits.lo, .limits.hi)] OutOfBounds { idx: usize, limits: Limits }, }`
-
A `From``#[from]`attribute.The variant using `#[from]`must not contain any other fields beyond the source error (and possibly a backtrace — see below). Usually`#[from]`fields are unnamed, but`#[from]`is allowed on a named field too.`#[derive(Error, Debug)] pub enum MyError { Io(#[from] io::Error), Glob(#[from] globset::Error), }`
-
The Error trait’s `source()``#[source]`attribute or is named`source`, if any. This is for identifying the underlying lower level error that caused your error.The `#[from]`attribute always implies that the same field is`#[source]`, so you don’t ever need to specify both attributes.Any error type that implements `std::error::Error`or dereferences to`dyn std::error::Error`will work as a source.`#[derive(Error, Debug)] pub struct MyError { msg: String, #[source] // optional if field name is `source` source: anyhow::Error, }`
-
The Error trait’s `provide()``Backtrace`, if any, as a`std::backtrace::Backtrace``Backtrace`in errors requires a nightly compiler with Rust version 1.73 or newer.`use std::backtrace::Backtrace; #[derive(Error, Debug)] pub struct MyError { msg: String, backtrace: Backtrace, // automatically detected }`
-
If a field is both a source (named `source`, or has`#[source]`or`#[from]`attribute)*and*is marked`#[backtrace]`, then the Error trait’s`provide()``provide`so that both layers of the error share the same backtrace. The`#[backtrace]`attribute requires a nightly compiler with Rust version 1.73 or newer.`#[derive(Error, Debug)] pub enum MyError { Io { #[backtrace] source: io::Error, }, }`
-
For variants that use `#[from]`and also contain a`Backtrace`field, a backtrace is captured from within the`From`impl.`#[derive(Error, Debug)] pub enum MyError { Io { #[from] source: io::Error, backtrace: Backtrace, }, }`
-
Errors may use `error(transparent)`to forward the source and`Display``#[derive(Error, Debug)] pub enum MyError { ... #[error(transparent)] Other(#[from] anyhow::Error), // source and Display delegate to anyhow::Error }`Another use case is hiding implementation details of an error representation behind an opaque error type, so that the representation is able to evolve without breaking the crate’s public API. `// PublicError is public, but opaque and easy to keep compatible. #[derive(Error, Debug)] #[error(transparent)] pub struct PublicError(#[from] ErrorRepr); impl PublicError { // Accessors for anything we do want to expose publicly. } // Private and free to change across minor version of the crate. #[derive(Error, Debug)] enum ErrorRepr { ... }`
-
See also the `anyhow`

---

# proptest - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/proptest/^1.9/

## Expand description

[§](https://docs.rs#proptest-reference-documentation)Proptest Reference Documentation

This is the reference documentation for the proptest API.

For documentation on how to get started with proptest and general usage
advice, please refer to the [Proptest Book](https://proptest-rs.github.io/proptest/intro.html).

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [arbitrary](https://docs.rs/arbitrary/index.html)
- Defines the `Arbitrary`trait and related free functions and type aliases.
- [array](https://docs.rs/array/index.html)
- Support for strategies producing fixed-length arrays.
- [bits](https://docs.rs/bits/index.html)
- Strategies for working with bit sets.
- [bool](https://docs.rs/bool/index.html)
- Strategies for generating `bool`values.
- [char](https://docs.rs/char/index.html)
- Strategies for generating `char`values.
- [collection](https://docs.rs/collection/index.html)
- Strategies for generating `std::collections`of values.
- [num](https://docs.rs/num/index.html)
- Strategies to generate numeric values (as opposed to integers used as bit fields).
- [option](https://docs.rs/option/index.html)
- Strategies for generating `std::Option`values.
- [path](https://docs.rs/path/index.html)- `std`
- Strategies for generating [`PathBuf`] and related path types.
- [prelude](https://docs.rs/prelude/index.html)
- Re-exports the most commonly-needed APIs of proptest.
- [range_](https://docs.rs/range_subset/index.html)- subset - `std`
- Strategies for generating values by taking samples of index ranges.
- [result](https://docs.rs/result/index.html)
- Strategies for combining delegate strategies into `std::Result`s.
- [sample](https://docs.rs/sample/index.html)
- Strategies for generating values by taking samples of collections.
- [strategy](https://docs.rs/strategy/index.html)
- Defines the core traits used by Proptest.
- [string](https://docs.rs/string/index.html)- `std`
- Strategies for generating strings and byte strings from regular expressions.
- [test_](https://docs.rs/test_runner/index.html)- runner
- State and functions for running proptest tests.
- [tuple](https://docs.rs/tuple/index.html)
- Support for combining strategies into tuples.

## Macros[§](https://docs.rs#macros)

- [prop_](https://docs.rs/macro.prop_assert.html)- assert
- Similar to `assert!`from std, but returns a test failure instead of panicking if the condition fails.
- [prop_](https://docs.rs/macro.prop_assert_eq.html)- assert_ - eq
- Similar to `assert_eq!`from std, but returns a test failure instead of panicking if the condition fails.
- [prop_](https://docs.rs/macro.prop_assert_ne.html)- assert_ - ne
- Similar to `assert_ne!`from std, but returns a test failure instead of panicking if the condition fails.
- [prop_](https://docs.rs/macro.prop_assume.html)- assume
- Rejects the test input if assumptions are not met.
- [prop_](https://docs.rs/macro.prop_compose.html)- compose
- Convenience to define functions which produce new strategies.
- [prop_](https://docs.rs/macro.prop_oneof.html)- oneof
- Produce a strategy which picks one of the listed choices.
- [proptest](https://docs.rs/macro.proptest.html)
- Easily define `proptest`tests.

## Attribute Macros[§](https://docs.rs#attributes)

- [property_](https://docs.rs/attr.property_test.html)- test - `attr-macro`
- The `property_test`procedural macro simplifies the creation of property-based tests using the`proptest`crate. This macro provides a more concise syntax for writing tests that automatically generate test cases based on properties.

# tempfile - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/tempfile/^3.10/

## Expand description

This is a library for creating temporary files and directories that are automatically deleted when no longer referenced (i.e., on drop).

- Use `tempfile()``std::fs::File`
- Use `NamedTempFile::new()`*named*temporary file that can be referred to its path.
- Use `tempdir()`
- Use `spooled_tempfile()`

[§](https://docs.rs#design)Design

This crate provides several approaches to creating temporary files and directories.
[ tempfile()](https://docs.rs/fn.tempfile.html) relies on the OS to remove the temporary file once the last handle is closed.

[and](https://docs.rs/struct.TempDir.html)

`TempDir`[both rely on Rust destructors for cleanup.](https://docs.rs/struct.NamedTempFile.html)

`NamedTempFile`[§](https://docs.rs#resource-leaking)Resource Leaking

`tempfile` will (almost) never fail to cleanup temporary resources. However `TempDir` and
`NamedTempFile` will fail if their destructors don’t run. This is because `tempfile` relies on
the OS to cleanup the underlying file, while `TempDir` and `NamedTempFile` rely on rust
destructors to do so. Destructors may fail to run if the process exits through an unhandled
signal interrupt (like `SIGINT`), or if the instance is declared statically (like with
[ lazy_static](https://github.com/rust-lang-nursery/lazy-static.rs/issues/62)), among other possible reasons.

[§](https://docs.rs#unexpected-file-deletion)Unexpected File Deletion

Most operating systems periodically clean up temporary files that haven’t been accessed recently
(often on the order of multiple days). This issue does not affect unnamed temporary files but
can invalidate the paths associated with named temporary files on Unix-like systems because the
temporary file can be unlinked from the filesystem while still open and in-use. See the
[temporary file cleaner](https://docs.rs#temporary-file-cleaners) section for more security implications.

[§](https://docs.rs#security)Security

This section discusses security issues relevant to Unix-like operating systems that use shared temporary directories by default. Importantly, it’s not relevant for Windows or macOS as both operating systems use private per-user temporary directories by default.

Applications can mitigate the issues described below by using [ env::override_temp_dir](https://docs.rs/env/fn.override_temp_dir.html) to
change the default temporary directory but should do so if and only if default the temporary
directory (

[) is unsuitable (is world readable, world writable, managed by a temporary file cleaner, etc.).](https://docs.rs/env/fn.temp_dir.html)

`env::temp_dir`[§](https://docs.rs#temporary-file-cleaners)Temporary File Cleaners

In the presence of pathological temporary file cleaner, relying on file paths is unsafe because a temporary file cleaner could delete the temporary file which an attacker could then replace.

This isn’t an issue for [ tempfile](https://docs.rs/fn.tempfile.html) as it doesn’t rely on file paths. However,

[and temporary directories](https://docs.rs/struct.NamedTempFile.html)

`NamedTempFile`*do*rely on file paths for

*some*operations. See the security documentation on the

[and the](https://docs.rs/struct.NamedTempFile.html)

`NamedTempFile`[types for more information.](https://docs.rs/struct.TempDir.html)

`TempDir`Mitigation:

- This is rarely an issue for short-lived files as temporary file cleaners usually only remove temporary files that haven’t been modified or accessed within many (10-30) days.
- Very long lived temporary files should be placed in directories not managed by temporary file cleaners.

[§](https://docs.rs#access-permissions)Access Permissions

Temporary *files* created with this library are private by default on all operating systems.
However, temporary *directories* are created with the default permissions and will therefore be
world-readable by default unless the user has changed their umask and/or default temporary
directory.

[§](https://docs.rs#denial-of-service)Denial of Service

If the file-name randomness ([ Builder::rand_bytes](https://docs.rs/struct.Builder.html#method.rand_bytes)) is too small and/or this crate is built
without the

`getrandom` feature, it may be possible for an attacker to predict the random file
names chosen by this library, preventing temporary file creation by creating temporary files
with these predicted file names. By default, this library mitigates this denial of service
attack by:- Defaulting to 6 random characters per temporary file forcing an attacker to create billions of files before random collisions are expected (at which point you probably have larger problems).
- Re-seeding the random filename generator from system randomness after 3 failed attempts to
create temporary a file (when the `getrandom`feature is enabled as it is by default on all major platforms).

[§](https://docs.rs#early-drop-pitfall)Early drop pitfall

Because `TempDir` and `NamedTempFile` rely on their destructors for cleanup, this can lead
to an unexpected early removal of the directory/file, usually when working with APIs which are
generic over `AsRef<Path>`. Consider the following example:

```
use tempfile::tempdir;
use std::process::Command;
// Create a directory inside of `env::temp_dir()`.
let temp_dir = tempdir()?;
// Spawn the `touch` command inside the temporary directory and collect the exit status
// Note that `temp_dir` is **not** moved into `current_dir`, but passed as a reference
let exit_status = Command::new("touch").arg("tmp").current_dir(&temp_dir).status()?;
assert!(exit_status.success());
```
This works because a reference to `temp_dir` is passed to `current_dir`, resulting in the
destructor of `temp_dir` being run after the `Command` has finished execution. Moving the
`TempDir` into the `current_dir` call would result in the `TempDir` being converted into
an internal representation, with the original value being dropped and the directory thus
being deleted, before the command can be executed.

The `touch` command would fail with an `No such file or directory` error.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

Create a temporary file and write some data into it:

```
use tempfile::tempfile;
use std::io::Write;
// Create a file inside of `env::temp_dir()`.
let mut file = tempfile()?;
writeln!(file, "Brian was here. Briefly.")?;
```
Create a named temporary file and open an independent file handle:

```
use tempfile::NamedTempFile;
use std::io::{Write, Read};
let text = "Brian was here. Briefly.";
// Create a file inside of `env::temp_dir()`.
let mut file1 = NamedTempFile::new()?;
// Re-open it.
let mut file2 = file1.reopen()?;
// Write some test data to the first handle.
file1.write_all(text.as_bytes())?;
// Read the test data using the second handle.
let mut buf = String::new();
file2.read_to_string(&mut buf)?;
assert_eq!(buf, text);
```
Create a temporary directory and add a file to it:

```
use tempfile::tempdir;
use std::fs::File;
use std::io::Write;
// Create a directory inside of `env::temp_dir()`.
let dir = tempdir()?;
let file_path = dir.path().join("my-temporary-note.txt");
let mut file = File::create(file_path)?;
writeln!(file, "Brian was here. Briefly.")?;
// By closing the `TempDir` explicitly, we can check that it has
// been deleted successfully. If we don't close it explicitly,
// the directory will still be deleted when `dir` goes out
// of scope, but we won't know whether deleting the directory
// succeeded.
drop(file);
dir.close()?;
```

# postings - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/postings/0.2.0/target-redirect/postings/

## Expand description

[§](https://docs.rs#postings)postings

A small inverted-index core built around postings lists.

[§](https://docs.rs#scope-deliberate)Scope (deliberate)

- This crate is **index-only**: it does not store document content.
- It supports **candidate generation**with**no false negatives**(a caller may choose to verify candidates with an exact matcher).
- It uses a Lucene-style mental model: immutable “segments” (here: append-only batches) and logical deletes.

[§](https://docs.rs#optional-modules)Optional modules

- `postings::codec`: low-level codecs (varint/gap) for postings payloads (in this repo).
- `postings::positional`(feature- `positional`): positional postings for phrase/proximity evaluation.
- `postings::raw`(feature- `raw-segment`): byte- and file-backed raw segment reader experiments.

[§](https://docs.rs#non-goals-for-now)Non-goals (for now)

- Full on-disk compaction
- Rich query language beyond candidate generation and sparse top-k scoring

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [codec](https://docs.rs/codec/index.html)
- Low-level codecs and iterator contracts for postings payloads.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Planner](https://docs.rs/struct.PlannerConfig.html)- Config
- Configuration for candidate planning / bailout.
- [Postings](https://docs.rs/struct.PostingsIndex.html)- Index
- A postings-based inverted index with segment-style updates.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Candidate](https://docs.rs/enum.CandidatePlan.html)- Plan
- Planner output for candidate generation.
- [Error](https://docs.rs/enum.Error.html)
- Errors returned by `postings`.

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

- [Weight](https://docs.rs/trait.Weight.html)
- Trait for term weight types in posting lists.

## Type Aliases[§](https://docs.rs#types)

- [DocId](https://docs.rs/type.DocId.html)
- Document identifier.

[200](#200)        if weight < self.min {
[201](#201)            self.min = weight;
[202](#202)        }
[203](#203)        if weight > self.max {

[210](#210)        let (_, first_weight) = postings.first()?;
[211](#211)        let mut bounds = Self::new(first_weight.to_f32());
[212](#212)        for &(_, weight) in &postings[1..] {
[213](#213)            bounds.update(weight.to_f32());
[214](#214)        }

[335](#335)    pub fn add_weighted_document(
[346](#346)        &mut self,
[347](#347)        doc_id: DocId,
[348](#348)        weighted_terms: &[(Term, W)],
[349](#349)    ) -> Result<(), Error> {
[350](#350)        if self.doc_segment.contains_key(&doc_id) {
[351](#351)            return Err(Error::DuplicateDocId(doc_id));
[352](#352)        }
[353](#353)
[354](#354)        let mut term_weights: HashMap<Term, W> = HashMap::new();
[355](#355)        let mut doc_length: u64 = 0;
[356](#356)        for (t, w) in weighted_terms {
[357](#357)            term_weights
[358](#358)                .entry(t.clone())
[359](#359)                .and_modify(|existing| existing.accumulate(*w))
[360](#360)                .or_insert(*w);
[361](#361)            doc_length += w.to_doc_len();
[362](#362)        }
[363](#363)
[364](#364)        self.index_document_inner(doc_id, term_weights, doc_length);
[365](#365)        Ok(())
[366](#366)    }
[367](#367)
[368](#368)    fn index_document_inner(
[372](#372)        &mut self,
[373](#373)        doc_id: DocId,
[374](#374)        term_weights: HashMap<Term, W>,
[375](#375)        doc_length: u64,
[376](#376)    ) {
[377](#377)        let mut doc_terms: Vec<Term> = term_weights.keys().cloned().collect();
[378](#378)        doc_terms.sort_unstable();
[379](#379)
[380](#380)        for (term, w) in &term_weights {
[384](#384)            let postings = self.global_postings.entry(term.clone()).or_default();
[385](#385)            match postings.binary_search_by_key(&doc_id, |(id, _)| *id) {
[386](#386)                Ok(i) => postings[i].1 = *w,
[387](#387)                Err(i) => postings.insert(i, (doc_id, *w)),
[388](#388)            }
[389](#389)            if !W::ALWAYS_NONNEGATIVE {
[390](#390)                let weight = w.to_f32();
[391](#391)                self.term_weight_bounds
[392](#392)                    .entry(term.clone())
[393](#393)                    .and_modify(|bounds| bounds.update(weight))
[394](#394)                    .or_insert_with(|| WeightBounds::new(weight));
[395](#395)            }
[396](#396)        }
[397](#397)
[398](#398)        for term in &doc_terms {
[400](#400)            *self.df.entry(term.clone()).or_insert(0) += 1;
[401](#401)        }
[402](#402)
[403](#403)        let mut seg = Segment::<Term, W>::default();
[405](#405)        seg.doc_terms.insert(doc_id, doc_terms); let seg_idx = self.segments.len();
[408](#408)        self.segments.push(seg);
[409](#409)        self.doc_segment.insert(doc_id, seg_idx);
[410](#410)        self.doc_len.insert(doc_id, doc_length as u32);
[411](#411)        self.total_doc_len += doc_length;
[412](#412)    }
[413](#413)}
[414](#414)
[415](#415)impl<Term> PostingsIndex<Term, u32>
[417](#417)where
[418](#418)    Term: Clone + Eq + Hash + Ord,
[419](#419){
[420](#420)    pub fn add_document(&mut self, doc_id: DocId, terms: &[Term]) -> Result<(), Error> {
[425](#425)        if self.doc_segment.contains_key(&doc_id) {
[426](#426)            return Err(Error::DuplicateDocId(doc_id));
[427](#427)        }
[428](#428)        let mut term_counts: HashMap<Term, u32> = HashMap::new();
[429](#429)        for t in terms {
[430](#430)            *term_counts.entry(t.clone()).or_insert(0) += 1;
[431](#431)        }
[432](#432)        let doc_length = terms.len() as u64;
[433](#433)        self.index_document_inner(doc_id, term_counts, doc_length);
[434](#434)        Ok(())
[435](#435)    }

[438](#438)impl<Term, W: Weight> PostingsIndex<Term, W>

[442](#442)    pub fn delete_document(&mut self, doc_id: DocId) -> bool {
[446](#446)        let seg_idx = match self.doc_segment.remove(&doc_id) {
[447](#447)            Some(i) => i,
[448](#448)            None => return false,
[449](#449)        };
[450](#450)        let doc_len = self.doc_len.remove(&doc_id).unwrap_or(0);
[451](#451)        self.total_doc_len = self.total_doc_len.saturating_sub(doc_len as u64);
[452](#452)
[453](#453)        let seg = &self.segments[seg_idx];
[454](#454)        if let Some(terms) = seg.doc_terms.get(&doc_id) {
[455](#455)            for term in terms {
[456](#456)                if let Some(df) = self.df.get_mut(term) {
[457](#457)                    *df = df.saturating_sub(1);
[458](#458)                    if *df == 0 {
[459](#459)                        self.df.remove(term);
[460](#460)                    }
[461](#461)                }
[462](#462)                if let Some(postings) = self.global_postings.get_mut(term) {
[463](#463)                    let removed_weight =
[464](#464)                        if let Ok(i) = postings.binary_search_by_key(&doc_id, |(id, _)| *id) {
[465](#465)                            let removed_weight = postings[i].1.to_f32();
[466](#466)                            postings.remove(i);
[467](#467)                            Some(removed_weight)
[468](#468)                        } else {
[469](#469)                            None
[470](#470)                        };
[471](#471)                    if postings.is_empty() {
[472](#472)                        self.global_postings.remove(term);
[473](#473)                        self.term_weight_bounds.remove(term);
[474](#474)                    } else if !W::ALWAYS_NONNEGATIVE {
[475](#475)                        if let Some(removed_weight) = removed_weight {
[476](#476)                            let recompute_bounds = match self.term_weight_bounds.get(term).copied()
[477](#477)                            {
[478](#478)                                Some(bounds) => {
[479](#479)                                    !removed_weight.is_finite()
[480](#480)                                        || removed_weight <= bounds.min
[481](#481)                                        || removed_weight >= bounds.max
[482](#482)                                }
[483](#483)                                None => true,
[484](#484)                            };
[485](#485)                            if recompute_bounds {
[486](#486)                                if let Some(bounds) = WeightBounds::from_postings(postings) {
[487](#487)                                    self.term_weight_bounds.insert(term.clone(), bounds);
[488](#488)                                }
[489](#489)                            }
[490](#490)                        }
[491](#491)                    }
[492](#492)                }
[493](#493)            }
[494](#494)        }
[495](#495)        true
[496](#496)    }

[498](#498)    pub fn term_frequency<Q>(&self, doc_id: DocId, term: &Q) -> W
[504](#504)    where
[505](#505)        Term: Borrow<Q>,
[506](#506)        Q: Hash + Eq + ?Sized,
[507](#507)    {
[508](#508)        if !self.doc_segment.contains_key(&doc_id) {
[510](#510)            return W::zero();
[511](#511)        }
[512](#512)        let postings = match self.global_postings.get(term) {
[513](#513)            Some(p) => p,
[514](#514)            None => return W::zero(),
[515](#515)        };
[516](#516)        match postings.binary_search_by_key(&doc_id, |(id, _)| *id) {
[517](#517)            Ok(i) => postings[i].1,
[518](#518)            Err(_) => W::zero(),
[519](#519)        }
[520](#520)    }

[522](#522)    pub fn candidates<Q>(&self, query_terms: &[Q]) -> Vec<DocId>
[524](#524)    where
[525](#525)        Term: Borrow<Q>,
[526](#526)        Q: Hash + Eq,
[527](#527)    {
[528](#528)        if query_terms.is_empty() {
[529](#529)            return Vec::new();
[530](#530)        }
[531](#531)        let mut lists: Vec<&[(DocId, W)]> = Vec::new();
[532](#532)        if query_terms.len() <= 32 {
[533](#533)            let mut seen_terms: Vec<&Q> = Vec::with_capacity(query_terms.len());
[534](#534)            'term: for term in query_terms {
[535](#535)                for seen in &seen_terms {
[536](#536)                    if *seen == term {
[537](#537)                        continue 'term;
[538](#538)                    }
[539](#539)                }
[540](#540)                seen_terms.push(term);
[541](#541)                if let Some(postings) = self.global_postings.get(term) {
[542](#542)                    if !postings.is_empty() {
[543](#543)                        lists.push(postings);
[544](#544)                    }
[545](#545)                }
[546](#546)            }
[547](#547)        } else {
[548](#548)            let mut seen_terms: HashSet<&Q> = HashSet::new();
[549](#549)            for term in query_terms {
[550](#550)                if !seen_terms.insert(term) {
[551](#551)                    continue;
[552](#552)                }
[553](#553)                if let Some(postings) = self.global_postings.get(term) {
[554](#554)                    if !postings.is_empty() {
[555](#555)                        lists.push(postings);
[556](#556)                    }
[557](#557)                }
[558](#558)            }
[559](#559)        }
[560](#560)        if lists.is_empty() {
[561](#561)            return Vec::new();
[562](#562)        }
[563](#563)        if lists.len() == 1 {
[564](#564)            return lists[0].iter().map(|(id, _)| *id).collect();
[565](#565)        }
[566](#566)
[567](#567)        if lists.len() >= 2 {
[570](#570)            let dense_slots = lists
[571](#571)                .iter()
[572](#572)                .filter_map(|postings| {
[573](#573)                    let (last_doc_id, _) = postings.last()?;
[574](#574)                    usize::try_from(*last_doc_id).ok()?.checked_add(1)
[575](#575)                })
[576](#576)                .max()
[577](#577)                .unwrap_or(0);
[578](#578)            let dense_limit = dense_scratch_limit(self.doc_len.len());
[579](#579)            if dense_slots <= dense_limit {
[580](#580)                let mut seen = vec![false; dense_slots];
[581](#581)                for postings in lists {
[582](#582)                    for &(doc_id, _) in postings {
[583](#583)                        seen[doc_id as usize] = true;
[584](#584)                    }
[585](#585)                }
[586](#586)                return seen
[587](#587)                    .into_iter()
[588](#588)                    .enumerate()
[589](#589)                    .filter_map(|(doc_id, hit)| hit.then_some(doc_id as DocId))
[590](#590)                    .collect();
[591](#591)            }
[592](#592)        }
[593](#593)
[594](#594)        lists.sort_by_key(|postings| postings.len());
[595](#595)        let mut lists = lists.into_iter();
[596](#596)        let mut out: Vec<DocId> = lists
[597](#597)            .next()
[598](#598)            .map(|postings| postings.iter().map(|(id, _)| *id).collect())
[599](#599)            .unwrap_or_default();
[600](#600)        for docs in lists {
[601](#601)            out = union_sorted_postings(&out, docs);
[602](#602)        }
[603](#603)        out
[604](#604)    }
[605](#605)
[606](#606)    pub fn candidates_all_terms<Q>(&self, query_terms: &[Q]) -> Vec<DocId>
[616](#616)    where
[617](#617)        Term: Borrow<Q>,
[618](#618)        Q: Hash + Eq,
[619](#619)    {
[620](#620)        if query_terms.is_empty() {
[621](#621)            return Vec::new();
[622](#622)        }
[623](#623)
[624](#624)        let mut lists: Vec<&[(DocId, W)]> = Vec::new();
[625](#625)        if query_terms.len() <= 32 {
[626](#626)            let mut uniq: Vec<&Q> = Vec::new();
[627](#627)            'term: for term in query_terms {
[628](#628)                for seen in &uniq {
[629](#629)                    if *seen == term {
[630](#630)                        continue 'term;
[631](#631)                    }
[632](#632)                }
[633](#633)                uniq.push(term);
[634](#634)                let Some(postings) = self.global_postings.get(term) else {
[635](#635)                    return Vec::new();
[636](#636)                };
[637](#637)                if postings.is_empty() {
[638](#638)                    return Vec::new();
[639](#639)                }
[640](#640)                lists.push(postings);
[641](#641)            }
[642](#642)        } else {
[643](#643)            let mut seen: HashSet<&Q> = HashSet::new();
[644](#644)            for t in query_terms {
[645](#645)                if seen.insert(t) {
[646](#646)                    let Some(postings) = self.global_postings.get(t) else {
[647](#647)                        return Vec::new();
[648](#648)                    };
[649](#649)                    if postings.is_empty() {
[650](#650)                        return Vec::new();
[651](#651)                    }
[652](#652)                    lists.push(postings);
[653](#653)                }
[654](#654)            }
[655](#655)        }
[656](#656)        if lists.is_empty() {
[657](#657)            return Vec::new();
[658](#658)        }
[659](#659)
[660](#660)        lists.sort_by_key(|postings| postings.len());
[663](#663)
[664](#664)        let mut acc: Vec<DocId> = lists[0].iter().map(|(id, _)| *id).collect();
[667](#667)
[668](#668)        for list in lists.into_iter().skip(1) {
[669](#669)            acc = intersect_sorted_postings(&acc, list);
[670](#670)            if acc.is_empty() {
[671](#671)                break;
[672](#672)            }
[673](#673)        }
[674](#674)        acc
[675](#675)    }
[676](#676)
[677](#677)    pub fn plan_candidates<Q>(&self, query_terms: &[Q], cfg: PlannerConfig) -> CandidatePlan
[683](#683)    where
[684](#684)        Term: Borrow<Q>,
[685](#685)        Q: Hash + Eq,
[686](#686)    {
[687](#687)        if query_terms.is_empty() {
[688](#688)            return CandidatePlan::Candidates(Vec::new());
[689](#689)        }
[690](#690)
[691](#691)        let n = self.num_docs();
[692](#692)        if n == 0 {
[693](#693)            return CandidatePlan::Candidates(Vec::new());
[694](#694)        }
[695](#695)
[696](#696)        let mut df_sum: u64 = 0;
[698](#698)        if query_terms.len() <= 32 {
[699](#699)            let mut seen_terms: Vec<&Q> = Vec::with_capacity(query_terms.len());
[700](#700)            'term: for term in query_terms {
[701](#701)                for seen in &seen_terms {
[702](#702)                    if *seen == term {
[703](#703)                        continue 'term;
[704](#704)                    }
[705](#705)                }
[706](#706)                seen_terms.push(term);
[707](#707)                df_sum = df_sum.saturating_add(self.df(term) as u64);
[708](#708)                if df_sum >= cfg.max_candidates as u64 {
[709](#709)                    return CandidatePlan::ScanAll;
[710](#710)                }
[711](#711)            }
[712](#712)        } else {
[713](#713)            let mut seen_terms: HashSet<&Q> = HashSet::new();
[714](#714)            for t in query_terms {
[715](#715)                if !seen_terms.insert(t) {
[716](#716)                    continue;
[717](#717)                }
[718](#718)                df_sum = df_sum.saturating_add(self.df(t) as u64);
[719](#719)                if df_sum >= cfg.max_candidates as u64 {
[720](#720)                    return CandidatePlan::ScanAll;
[721](#721)                }
[722](#722)            }
[723](#723)        }
[724](#724)
[725](#725)        let ratio = (df_sum as f32) / (n as f32);
[726](#726)        if ratio > cfg.max_candidate_ratio {
[727](#727)            return CandidatePlan::ScanAll;
[728](#728)        }
[729](#729)
[730](#730)        CandidatePlan::Candidates(self.candidates(query_terms))
[731](#731)    }
[732](#732)
[733](#733)    pub fn postings_iter<'a, Q>(&'a self, term: &'a Q) -> impl Iterator<Item = (DocId, W)> + 'a
[738](#738)    where
[739](#739)        Term: Borrow<Q>,
[740](#740)        Q: Hash + Eq + ?Sized,
[741](#741)    {
[742](#742)        self.global_postings
[743](#743)            .get(term)
[744](#744)            .into_iter()
[745](#745)            .flat_map(|v| v.iter().copied())
[746](#746)            .filter(|(doc_id, _)| self.doc_segment.contains_key(doc_id))
[747](#747)    }
[748](#748)
[749](#749)    fn weight_bounds<Q>(&self, term: &Q, postings: &[(DocId, W)]) -> Option<WeightBounds>
[750](#750)    where
[751](#751)        Term: Borrow<Q>,
[752](#752)        Q: Hash + Eq + ?Sized,
[753](#753)    {
[754](#754)        self.term_weight_bounds
[755](#755)            .get(term)
[756](#756)            .copied()
[757](#757)            .or_else(|| WeightBounds::from_postings(postings))
[758](#758)    }
[759](#759)
[760](#760)    fn contributions_are_nonnegative<Q>(
[761](#761)        &self,
[762](#762)        term: &Q,
[763](#763)        postings: &[(DocId, W)],
[764](#764)        query_weight: f32,
[765](#765)    ) -> bool
[766](#766)    where
[767](#767)        Term: Borrow<Q>,
[768](#768)        Q: Hash + Eq + ?Sized,
[769](#769)    {
[770](#770)        if !query_weight.is_finite() {
[771](#771)            return false;
[772](#772)        }
[773](#773)        if W::ALWAYS_NONNEGATIVE {
[774](#774)            return query_weight >= 0.0;
[775](#775)        }
[776](#776)        self.weight_bounds(term, postings)
[777](#777)            .is_some_and(|bounds| bounds.contribution_is_nonnegative(query_weight))
[778](#778)    }
[779](#779)
[780](#780)    pub fn top_k_weighted<Q>(&self, query_terms: &[(&Q, f32)], k: usize) -> Vec<(DocId, f32)>
[786](#786)    where
[787](#787)        Term: Borrow<Q>,
[788](#788)        Q: Hash + Eq + ?Sized,
[789](#789)    {
[790](#790)        if k == 0 || query_terms.is_empty() {
[791](#791)            return Vec::new();
[792](#792)        }
[793](#793)        if query_terms.len() == 1 {
[794](#794)            let (term, query_weight) = query_terms[0];
[795](#795)            if query_weight == 0.0 {
[796](#796)                return Vec::new();
[797](#797)            }
[798](#798)            let Some(postings) = self.global_postings.get(term) else {
[799](#799)                return Vec::new();
[800](#800)            };
[801](#801)            return top_k_single_postings(postings, query_weight, k);
[802](#802)        }
[803](#803)
[804](#804)        let mut lists = Vec::with_capacity(query_terms.len());
[805](#805)        let mut total_postings = 0usize;
[806](#806)        if query_terms.len() <= 32 {
[809](#809)            let mut query_weights: Vec<(&Q, f32)> = Vec::with_capacity(query_terms.len());
[810](#810)            'term: for &(term, weight) in query_terms {
[811](#811)                if weight == 0.0 {
[812](#812)                    continue;
[813](#813)                }
[814](#814)                for (existing_term, existing_weight) in &mut query_weights {
[815](#815)                    if *existing_term == term {
[816](#816)                        *existing_weight += weight;
[817](#817)                        continue 'term;
[818](#818)                    }
[819](#819)                }
[820](#820)                query_weights.push((term, weight));
[821](#821)            }
[822](#822)            if query_weights.is_empty() {
[823](#823)                return Vec::new();
[824](#824)            }
[825](#825)            for (term, query_weight) in query_weights {
[826](#826)                if query_weight == 0.0 {
[827](#827)                    continue;
[828](#828)                }
[829](#829)                let Some(postings) = self.global_postings.get(term) else {
[830](#830)                    continue;
[831](#831)                };
[832](#832)                if postings.is_empty() {
[833](#833)                    continue;
[834](#834)                }
[835](#835)                total_postings = total_postings.saturating_add(postings.len());
[836](#836)                lists.push((term, postings.as_slice(), query_weight));
[837](#837)            }
[838](#838)        } else {
[839](#839)            let mut query_weights: HashMap<&Q, f32> = HashMap::new();
[840](#840)            for &(term, weight) in query_terms {
[841](#841)                if weight == 0.0 {
[842](#842)                    continue;
[843](#843)                }
[844](#844)                *query_weights.entry(term).or_insert(0.0) += weight;
[845](#845)            }
[846](#846)            if query_weights.is_empty() {
[847](#847)                return Vec::new();
[848](#848)            }
[849](#849)            for (term, query_weight) in query_weights {
[850](#850)                if query_weight == 0.0 {
[851](#851)                    continue;
[852](#852)                }
[853](#853)                let Some(postings) = self.global_postings.get(term) else {
[854](#854)                    continue;
[855](#855)                };
[856](#856)                if postings.is_empty() {
[857](#857)                    continue;
[858](#858)                }
[859](#859)                total_postings = total_postings.saturating_add(postings.len());
[860](#860)                lists.push((term, postings.as_slice(), query_weight));
[861](#861)            }
[862](#862)        }
[863](#863)        if lists.is_empty() {
[864](#864)            return Vec::new();
[865](#865)        }
[866](#866)
[867](#867)        if lists.len() == 1 {
[868](#868)            let (_, postings, query_weight) = lists[0];
[869](#869)            return top_k_single_postings(postings, query_weight, k);
[870](#870)        }
[871](#871)
[872](#872)        let dense_slots = lists
[873](#873)            .iter()
[874](#874)            .filter_map(|(_, postings, _)| {
[875](#875)                let (last_doc_id, _) = postings.last()?;
[876](#876)                usize::try_from(*last_doc_id).ok()?.checked_add(1)
[877](#877)            })
[878](#878)            .max()
[879](#879)            .unwrap_or(0);
[880](#880)        let dense_limit = dense_scratch_limit(self.doc_len.len());
[881](#881)        if dense_slots <= dense_limit {
[882](#882)            let mut scores = vec![0.0; dense_slots];
[883](#883)            let mut touched = Vec::with_capacity(total_postings.min(self.doc_len.len()));
[884](#884)
[885](#885)            let contributions_are_nonnegative =
[886](#886)                lists.iter().all(|(term, postings, query_weight)| {
[887](#887)                    self.contributions_are_nonnegative(*term, postings, *query_weight)
[888](#888)                });
[889](#889)
[890](#890)            if contributions_are_nonnegative {
[891](#891)                for (_, postings, query_weight) in lists {
[892](#892)                    for &(doc_id, doc_weight) in postings {
[893](#893)                        let contribution = query_weight * doc_weight.to_f32();
[894](#894)                        if contribution == 0.0 {
[895](#895)                            continue;
[896](#896)                        }
[897](#897)                        let slot = doc_id as usize;
[898](#898)                        if scores[slot] == 0.0 {
[899](#899)                            touched.push(doc_id);
[900](#900)                        }
[901](#901)                        scores[slot] += contribution;
[902](#902)                    }
[903](#903)                }
[904](#904)            } else {
[905](#905)                let mut seen = vec![false; dense_slots];
[906](#906)                for (_, postings, query_weight) in lists {
[907](#907)                    for &(doc_id, doc_weight) in postings {
[908](#908)                        let contribution = query_weight * doc_weight.to_f32();
[909](#909)                        if contribution == 0.0 {
[910](#910)                            continue;
[911](#911)                        }
[912](#912)                        let slot = doc_id as usize;
[913](#913)                        if !seen[slot] {
[914](#914)                            seen[slot] = true;
[915](#915)                            touched.push(doc_id);
[916](#916)                        }
[917](#917)                        scores[slot] += contribution;
[918](#918)                    }
[919](#919)                }
[920](#920)            }
[921](#921)
[922](#922)            return top_k_scored_docs(
[923](#923)                touched
[924](#924)                    .into_iter()
[925](#925)                    .map(|doc_id| (doc_id, scores[doc_id as usize])),
[926](#926)                k,
[927](#927)            );
[928](#928)        }
[929](#929)
[930](#930)        let mut scores: HashMap<DocId, f32> =
[931](#931)            HashMap::with_capacity(total_postings.min(self.doc_len.len()));
[932](#932)        for (_, postings, query_weight) in lists {
[933](#933)            for &(doc_id, doc_weight) in postings {
[934](#934)                let contribution = query_weight * doc_weight.to_f32();
[935](#935)                if contribution != 0.0 {
[936](#936)                    *scores.entry(doc_id).or_insert(0.0) += contribution;
[937](#937)                }
[938](#938)            }
[939](#939)        }
[940](#940)
[941](#941)        top_k_scored_docs(scores, k)
[942](#942)    }
[943](#943)

[964](#964)    #[cfg(feature = "persistence")]
[971](#971)    pub fn save_durable<D: durability::Directory + ?Sized>(
[972](#972)        &self,
[973](#973)        dir: &D,
[974](#974)        path: &str,
[975](#975)    ) -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>>
[976](#976)    where
[977](#977)        Term: serde::Serialize,
[978](#978)        W: serde::Serialize,
[979](#979)    {
[980](#980)        let bytes = postcard::to_allocvec(self)?;
[981](#981)        dir.atomic_write_durable(path, &bytes)?;
[982](#982)        Ok(())
[983](#983)    }
[984](#984)
[985](#985)    #[cfg(feature = "persistence")]
[987](#987)    pub fn load<D: durability::Directory + ?Sized>(
[988](#988)        dir: &D,
[989](#989)        path: &str,
[990](#990)    ) -> Result<Self, Box<dyn std::error::Error>>
[991](#991)    where
[992](#992)        for<'de> Term: serde::Deserialize<'de>,
[993](#993)        for<'de> W: serde::Deserialize<'de>,
[994](#994)    {
[995](#995)        use std::io::Read;
[996](#996)
[997](#997)        let mut f = dir.open_file(path)?;
[998](#998)        let mut bytes = Vec::new();
[999](#999)        f.read_to_end(&mut bytes)?;
[1000](#1000)        let idx: Self = postcard::from_bytes(&bytes)?;
[1001](#1001)        Ok(idx)
[1002](#1002)    }
[1003](#1003)}
[1004](#1004)
[1005](#1005)fn union_sorted_postings<W>(a: &[DocId], b: &[(DocId, W)]) -> Vec<DocId> {
[1006](#1006)    let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(a.len().saturating_add(b.len()));
[1007](#1007)    let mut i = 0usize;
[1008](#1008)    let mut j = 0usize;
[1009](#1009)
[1010](#1010)    while i < a.len() && j < b.len() {
[1011](#1011)        match a[i].cmp(&b[j].0) {
[1012](#1012)            std::cmp::Ordering::Equal => {
[1013](#1013)                push_unique(&mut out, a[i]);
[1014](#1014)                i += 1;
[1015](#1015)                j += 1;
[1016](#1016)            }
[1017](#1017)            std::cmp::Ordering::Less => {
[1018](#1018)                push_unique(&mut out, a[i]);
[1019](#1019)                i += 1;
[1020](#1020)            }
[1021](#1021)            std::cmp::Ordering::Greater => {
[1022](#1022)                push_unique(&mut out, b[j].0);
[1023](#1023)                j += 1;
[1024](#1024)            }
[1025](#1025)        }
[1026](#1026)    }
[1027](#1027)    while i < a.len() {
[1028](#1028)        push_unique(&mut out, a[i]);
[1029](#1029)        i += 1;
[1030](#1030)    }
[1031](#1031)    while j < b.len() {
[1032](#1032)        push_unique(&mut out, b[j].0);
[1033](#1033)        j += 1;
[1034](#1034)    }
[1035](#1035)    out
[1036](#1036)}
[1037](#1037)
[1038](#1038)#[inline]
[1039](#1039)fn push_unique(out: &mut Vec<DocId>, doc_id: DocId) {
[1040](#1040)    if out.last().copied() != Some(doc_id) {
[1041](#1041)        out.push(doc_id);
[1042](#1042)    }
[1043](#1043)}
[1044](#1044)
[1045](#1045)fn intersect_sorted_postings<W>(a: &[DocId], b: &[(DocId, W)]) -> Vec<DocId> {
[1046](#1046)    let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(a.len().min(b.len()));
[1047](#1047)    if a.is_empty() || b.is_empty() {
[1048](#1048)        return out;
[1049](#1049)    }
[1050](#1050)    let min_len = a.len().min(b.len());
[1051](#1051)    let max_len = a.len().max(b.len());
[1052](#1052)    if max_len <= min_len.saturating_mul(8) {
[1053](#1053)        let mut i = 0usize;
[1054](#1054)        let mut j = 0usize;
[1055](#1055)        while i < a.len() && j < b.len() {
[1056](#1056)            match a[i].cmp(&b[j].0) {
[1057](#1057)                std::cmp::Ordering::Equal => {
[1058](#1058)                    out.push(a[i]);
[1059](#1059)                    i += 1;
[1060](#1060)                    j += 1;
[1061](#1061)                }
[1062](#1062)                std::cmp::Ordering::Less => i += 1,
[1063](#1063)                std::cmp::Ordering::Greater => j += 1,
[1064](#1064)            }
[1065](#1065)        }
[1066](#1066)        return out;
[1067](#1067)    }
[1068](#1068)
[1069](#1069)    let mut i = 0usize;
[1075](#1075)    let mut j = 0usize;
[1076](#1076)
[1077](#1077)    while i < a.len() && j < b.len() {
[1078](#1078)        match a[i].cmp(&b[j].0) {
[1079](#1079)            std::cmp::Ordering::Equal => {
[1080](#1080)                out.push(a[i]);
[1081](#1081)                i += 1;
[1082](#1082)                j += 1;
[1083](#1083)            }
[1084](#1084)            std::cmp::Ordering::Less => {
[1085](#1085)                i = gallop_forward(a, i, b[j].0);
[1087](#1087)            }
[1088](#1088)            std::cmp::Ordering::Greater => {
[1089](#1089)                j = gallop_forward_postings(b, j, a[i]);
[1091](#1091)            }
[1092](#1092)        }
[1093](#1093)    }
[1094](#1094)    out
[1095](#1095)}
[1096](#1096)
[1097](#1097)#[inline]
[1101](#1101)fn gallop_forward(list: &[DocId], start: usize, target: DocId) -> usize {
[1102](#1102)    if start >= list.len() || list[start] >= target {
[1103](#1103)        return start;
[1104](#1104)    }
[1105](#1105)    let mut step = 1usize;
[1106](#1106)    while start + step < list.len() && list[start + step] < target {
[1108](#1108)        step <<= 1;
[1109](#1109)    }
[1110](#1110)    let lo = start + (step >> 1);
[1112](#1112)    let hi = (start + step).min(list.len());
[1113](#1113)    match list[lo..hi].binary_search(&target) {
[1114](#1114)        Ok(k) => lo + k,
[1115](#1115)        Err(k) => lo + k,
[1116](#1116)    }
[1117](#1117)}
[1118](#1118)
[1119](#1119)#[inline]
[1121](#1121)fn gallop_forward_postings<W>(list: &[(DocId, W)], start: usize, target: DocId) -> usize {
[1122](#1122)    if start >= list.len() || list[start].0 >= target {
[1123](#1123)        return start;
[1124](#1124)    }
[1125](#1125)    let mut step = 1usize;
[1126](#1126)    while start + step < list.len() && list[start + step].0 < target {
[1127](#1127)        step <<= 1;
[1128](#1128)    }
[1129](#1129)    let lo = start + (step >> 1);
[1130](#1130)    let hi = (start + step).min(list.len());
[1131](#1131)    match list[lo..hi].binary_search_by_key(&target, |(id, _)| *id) {
[1132](#1132)        Ok(k) => lo + k,
[1133](#1133)        Err(k) => lo + k,
[1134](#1134)    }
[1135](#1135)}
[1136](#1136)
[1137](#1137)#[inline]
[1138](#1138)fn cmp_doc_scores(a: &(DocId, f32), b: &(DocId, f32)) -> std::cmp::Ordering {
[1139](#1139)    b.1.total_cmp(&a.1).then_with(|| a.0.cmp(&b.0))
[1140](#1140)}
[1141](#1141)
[1142](#1142)#[inline]
[1143](#1143)fn keep_top_k(ranked: &mut Vec<(DocId, f32)>, k: usize) {
[1144](#1144)    if ranked.len() > k {
[1145](#1145)        ranked.select_nth_unstable_by(k, cmp_doc_scores);
[1146](#1146)        ranked.truncate(k);
[1147](#1147)    }
[1148](#1148)    ranked.sort_by(cmp_doc_scores);
[1149](#1149)}
[1150](#1150)
[1151](#1151)fn top_k_scored_docs<I>(docs: I, k: usize) -> Vec<(DocId, f32)>
[1152](#1152)where
[1153](#1153)    I: IntoIterator<Item = (DocId, f32)>,
[1154](#1154){
[1155](#1155)    if k == 0 {
[1156](#1156)        return Vec::new();
[1157](#1157)    }
[1158](#1158)
[1159](#1159)    let mut ranked: Vec<(DocId, f32)> = Vec::with_capacity(k);
[1160](#1160)    let mut sorted = false;
[1161](#1161)    for doc in docs {
[1162](#1162)        if doc.1 == 0.0 {
[1163](#1163)            continue;
[1164](#1164)        }
[1165](#1165)        if ranked.len() < k {
[1166](#1166)            ranked.push(doc);
[1167](#1167)            continue;
[1168](#1168)        }
[1169](#1169)        if !sorted {
[1170](#1170)            ranked.sort_by(cmp_doc_scores);
[1171](#1171)            sorted = true;
[1172](#1172)        }
[1173](#1173)        if cmp_doc_scores(&doc, ranked.last().expect("top-k buffer is full")).is_lt() {
[1174](#1174)            let last = ranked.len() - 1;
[1175](#1175)            ranked[last] = doc;
[1176](#1176)            let mut i = last;
[1177](#1177)            while i > 0 && cmp_doc_scores(&ranked[i], &ranked[i - 1]).is_lt() {
[1178](#1178)                ranked.swap(i, i - 1);
[1179](#1179)                i -= 1;
[1180](#1180)            }
[1181](#1181)        }
[1182](#1182)    }
[1183](#1183)    if !sorted {
[1184](#1184)        ranked.sort_by(cmp_doc_scores);
[1185](#1185)    }
[1186](#1186)    ranked
[1187](#1187)}
[1188](#1188)
[1189](#1189)fn top_k_single_postings<W: Weight>(
[1190](#1190)    postings: &[(DocId, W)],
[1191](#1191)    query_weight: f32,
[1192](#1192)    k: usize,
[1193](#1193)) -> Vec<(DocId, f32)> {
[1194](#1194)    if k == 0 {
[1195](#1195)        return Vec::new();
[1196](#1196)    }
[1197](#1197)    if postings.len() > k {
[1198](#1198)        let mut ranked: Vec<(DocId, f32)> = Vec::with_capacity(k);
[1199](#1199)        let mut sorted = false;
[1200](#1200)        for &(doc_id, doc_weight) in postings {
[1201](#1201)            let score = query_weight * doc_weight.to_f32();
[1202](#1202)            if score == 0.0 {
[1203](#1203)                continue;
[1204](#1204)            }
[1205](#1205)            if ranked.len() < k {
[1206](#1206)                ranked.push((doc_id, score));
[1207](#1207)                continue;
[1208](#1208)            }
[1209](#1209)            if !sorted {
[1210](#1210)                ranked.sort_by(cmp_doc_scores);
[1211](#1211)                sorted = true;
[1212](#1212)            }
[1213](#1213)            let candidate = (doc_id, score);
[1214](#1214)            if cmp_doc_scores(&candidate, ranked.last().expect("top-k buffer is full")).is_lt() {
[1215](#1215)                let last = ranked.len() - 1;
[1216](#1216)                ranked[last] = candidate;
[1217](#1217)                let mut i = last;
[1218](#1218)                while i > 0 && cmp_doc_scores(&ranked[i], &ranked[i - 1]).is_lt() {
[1219](#1219)                    ranked.swap(i, i - 1);
[1220](#1220)                    i -= 1;
[1221](#1221)                }
[1222](#1222)            }
[1223](#1223)        }
[1224](#1224)        if !sorted {
[1225](#1225)            ranked.sort_by(cmp_doc_scores);
[1226](#1226)        }
[1227](#1227)        return ranked;
[1228](#1228)    }
[1229](#1229)
[1230](#1230)    let mut ranked = Vec::with_capacity(postings.len());
[1231](#1231)    for &(doc_id, doc_weight) in postings {
[1232](#1232)        let score = query_weight * doc_weight.to_f32();
[1233](#1233)        if score != 0.0 {
[1234](#1234)            ranked.push((doc_id, score));
[1235](#1235)        }
[1236](#1236)    }
[1237](#1237)    keep_top_k(&mut ranked, k);
[1238](#1238)    ranked
[1239](#1239)}

[1383](#1383)        fn candidates_have_no_false_negatives(
[1384](#1384)            docs in prop::collection::vec(
[1385](#1385)                prop::collection::vec("[a-z]{1,6}", 0..20),
[1386](#1386)                0..30
[1387](#1387)            ),
[1388](#1388)            query in prop::collection::vec("[a-z]{1,6}", 0..10),
[1389](#1389)        ) {
[1390](#1390)            let mut idx: PostingsIndex<String> = PostingsIndex::new();
[1391](#1391)            for (i, terms) in docs.iter().enumerate() {
[1392](#1392)                let terms: Vec<String> = terms.to_vec();
[1393](#1393)                idx.add_document(i as DocId, &terms).unwrap();
[1394](#1394)            }
[1395](#1395)
[1396](#1396)            let q_terms: Vec<String> = query.to_vec();
[1397](#1397)            let cands = idx.candidates(&q_terms);
[1398](#1398)            let cand_set: std::collections::HashSet<DocId> = cands.into_iter().collect();
[1399](#1399)
[1400](#1400)            for doc_id in idx.document_ids() {
[1402](#1402)                let mut hits = false;
[1403](#1403)                for t in &q_terms {
[1404](#1404)                    if idx.term_frequency(doc_id, t) > 0 {
[1405](#1405)                        hits = true;
[1406](#1406)                        break;
[1407](#1407)                    }
[1408](#1408)                }
[1409](#1409)                if hits {
[1410](#1410)                    prop_assert!(cand_set.contains(&doc_id));
[1411](#1411)                }
[1412](#1412)            }
[1413](#1413)        }

[1436](#1436)        idx.add_document(0, &[1, 2, 2, 3]).unwrap();
[1437](#1437)        idx.add_document(1, &[2, 4]).unwrap();
[1438](#1438)        assert_eq!(idx.df(&2u32), 2);
[1439](#1439)        assert_eq!(idx.term_frequency(0, &2u32), 2);
[1440](#1440)        assert_eq!(idx.term_frequency(1, &2u32), 1);
[1441](#1441)
[1442](#1442)        let plan = idx.plan_candidates(
[1445](#1445)            &[2u32],
[1446](#1446)            PlannerConfig {
[1447](#1447)                max_candidate_ratio: 1.0,
[1448](#1448)                max_candidates: 10_000,
[1449](#1449)            },
[1450](#1450)        );
[1451](#1451)        match plan {
[1452](#1452)            CandidatePlan::Candidates(cands) => {
[1453](#1453)                assert!(cands.contains(&0));
[1454](#1454)                assert!(cands.contains(&1));
[1455](#1455)            }
[1456](#1456)            CandidatePlan::ScanAll => panic!("unexpected bailout for tiny corpus"),
[1457](#1457)        }
[1458](#1458)    }
[1459](#1459)

[1492](#1492)    proptest! {
[1493](#1493)        #[test]
[1494](#1494)        fn candidates_all_terms_have_no_false_negatives(
[1495](#1495)            docs in prop::collection::vec(
[1496](#1496)                prop::collection::vec("[a-z]{1,6}", 0..20),
[1497](#1497)                0..30
[1498](#1498)            ),
[1499](#1499)            query in prop::collection::vec("[a-z]{1,6}", 0..10),
[1500](#1500)        ) {
[1501](#1501)            let mut idx: PostingsIndex<String> = PostingsIndex::new();
[1502](#1502)            for (i, terms) in docs.iter().enumerate() {
[1503](#1503)                let terms: Vec<String> = terms.to_vec();
[1504](#1504)                idx.add_document(i as DocId, &terms).unwrap();
[1505](#1505)            }
[1506](#1506)
[1507](#1507)            let q_terms: Vec<String> = query.to_vec();
[1508](#1508)            let cands = idx.candidates_all_terms(&q_terms);
[1509](#1509)            let cand_set: std::collections::HashSet<DocId> = cands.into_iter().collect();
[1510](#1510)
[1511](#1511)            let mut uniq: std::collections::HashSet<&String> = std::collections::HashSet::new();
[1514](#1514)            for t in &q_terms {
[1515](#1515)                uniq.insert(t);
[1516](#1516)            }
[1517](#1517)            for doc_id in idx.document_ids() {
[1518](#1518)                let mut ok = !uniq.is_empty();
[1519](#1519)                for t in &uniq {
[1520](#1520)                    if idx.term_frequency(doc_id, t.as_str()) == 0 {
[1521](#1521)                        ok = false;
[1522](#1522)                        break;
[1523](#1523)                    }
[1524](#1524)                }
[1525](#1525)                if ok {
[1526](#1526)                    prop_assert!(cand_set.contains(&doc_id));
[1527](#1527)                }
[1528](#1528)            }
[1529](#1529)        }
[1530](#1530)    }
[1531](#1531)
[1532](#1532)    proptest! {
[1533](#1533)        #[test]
[1534](#1534)        fn plan_candidates_candidates_respects_thresholds(
[1535](#1535)            docs in prop::collection::vec(
[1536](#1536)                prop::collection::vec("[a-z]{1,6}", 0..30),
[1537](#1537)                0..60
[1538](#1538)            ),
[1539](#1539)            query in prop::collection::vec("[a-z]{1,6}", 0..12),
[1540](#1540)            max_ratio in 0.05f32..1.0f32,
[1541](#1541)            max_abs in 1u32..5000u32,
[1542](#1542)        ) {
[1543](#1543)            let mut idx: PostingsIndex<String> = PostingsIndex::new();
[1544](#1544)            for (i, doc) in docs.iter().enumerate() {
[1545](#1545)                let terms: Vec<String> = doc.to_vec();
[1546](#1546)                idx.add_document(i as DocId, &terms).unwrap();
[1547](#1547)            }
[1548](#1548)
[1549](#1549)            let q_terms: Vec<String> = query.to_vec();
[1550](#1550)            let cfg = PlannerConfig { max_candidate_ratio: max_ratio, max_candidates: max_abs };
[1551](#1551)
[1552](#1552)            let plan = idx.plan_candidates(&q_terms, cfg);
[1553](#1553)            if let CandidatePlan::Candidates(_cands) = plan {
[1554](#1554)                let n = idx.num_docs();
[1557](#1557)                if n == 0 || q_terms.is_empty() {
[1558](#1558)                    return Ok(());
[1559](#1559)                }
[1560](#1560)
[1561](#1561)                let mut seen: std::collections::HashSet<&String> = std::collections::HashSet::new();
[1562](#1562)                let mut df_sum: u64 = 0;
[1563](#1563)                for t in &q_terms {
[1564](#1564)                    if !seen.insert(t) { continue; }
[1565](#1565)                    df_sum = df_sum.saturating_add(idx.df(t) as u64);
[1566](#1566)                }
[1567](#1567)
[1568](#1568)                prop_assert!(df_sum < (cfg.max_candidates as u64));
[1569](#1569)                prop_assert!((df_sum as f32) / (n as f32) <= cfg.max_candidate_ratio);
[1570](#1570)            }
[1571](#1571)        }
[1572](#1572)    }
[1573](#1573)

[1661](#1661)        idx.add_weighted_document(
[1662](#1662)            1,
[1663](#1663)            &[

[1694](#1694)        assert_eq!(ranked[0].0, 2);

[1696](#1696)        assert_eq!(ranked[1].0, 3);
[1697](#1697)        assert!((ranked[1].1 - 4.8).abs() < 1e-6);
[1698](#1698)        assert_eq!(ranked[2].0, 0);
[1699](#1699)        assert!((ranked[2].1 - 2.7).abs() < 1e-6);
[1700](#1700)    }

[1865](#1865)
[1866](#1866)    fn exact_sparse_top_k(
[1867](#1867)        docs: &[(DocId, std::collections::HashMap<u8, f32>)],
[1868](#1868)        query_terms: &[(u8, f32)],
[1869](#1869)        k: usize,
[1870](#1870)    ) -> Vec<(DocId, f32)> {
[1871](#1871)        if k == 0 || query_terms.is_empty() {
[1872](#1872)            return Vec::new();
[1873](#1873)        }
[1874](#1874)
[1875](#1875)        let mut query_weights: std::collections::HashMap<u8, f32> =
[1876](#1876)            std::collections::HashMap::new();
[1877](#1877)        for &(term, weight) in query_terms {
[1878](#1878)            if weight != 0.0 {
[1879](#1879)                *query_weights.entry(term).or_insert(0.0) += weight;
[1880](#1880)            }
[1881](#1881)        }
[1882](#1882)
[1883](#1883)        let mut scored = Vec::new();
[1884](#1884)        for &(doc_id, ref doc_weights) in docs {
[1885](#1885)            let mut score = 0.0;
[1886](#1886)            for (&term, &query_weight) in &query_weights {
[1887](#1887)                if let Some(&doc_weight) = doc_weights.get(&term) {
[1888](#1888)                    let contribution = query_weight * doc_weight;
[1889](#1889)                    if contribution != 0.0 {
[1890](#1890)                        score += contribution;
[1891](#1891)                    }
[1892](#1892)                }
[1893](#1893)            }
[1894](#1894)            if score != 0.0 {
[1895](#1895)                scored.push((doc_id, score));
[1896](#1896)            }
[1897](#1897)        }
[1898](#1898)        scored.sort_by(|left, right| {
[1899](#1899)            right
[1900](#1900)                .1
[1901](#1901)                .total_cmp(&left.1)
[1902](#1902)                .then_with(|| left.0.cmp(&right.0))
[1903](#1903)        });
[1904](#1904)        scored.truncate(k);
[1905](#1905)        scored
[1906](#1906)    }
[1907](#1907)
[1908](#1908)    fn quarter_weight(raw: u8) -> f32 {
[1909](#1909)        (raw as f32) * 0.25
[1910](#1910)    }
[1911](#1911)
[1912](#1912)    fn signed_quarter_weight(raw: i8) -> f32 {
[1913](#1913)        (raw as f32) * 0.25
[1914](#1914)    }
[1915](#1915)

[1917](#1917)        #[test]
[1918](#1918)        fn top_k_weighted_matches_exact_sparse_dot_product(
[1919](#1919)            docs in prop::collection::vec(

[1926](#1926)        ) {
[1927](#1927)            let mut idx: PostingsIndex<String, f32> = PostingsIndex::new();
[1928](#1928)            let mut oracle_docs = Vec::new();
[1929](#1929)

[1931](#1931)                let doc_id = (i as DocId) * stride;
[1932](#1932)                let weighted_terms: Vec<(String, f32)> = doc_terms

[1944](#1944)

[1952](#1952)                .collect();

# postings::codec - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/postings/0.2.0/postings/codec/index.html

## Expand description

Low-level codecs and iterator contracts for postings payloads.

This module holds *mechanical* building blocks:

- integer encodings (varint, delta/gap)
- decode iterators
- succinct monotone sequences (optional, via `sbits`)

It intentionally does **not** define an inverted index; it exists so multiple
index structures can share the same low-level encoding/decoding logic.

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [varint](https://docs.rs/varint/index.html)
- Simple varint encoding for `u32`.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Error](https://docs.rs/enum.Error.html)
- Errors for postings codecs.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [gaps_](https://docs.rs/fn.gaps_from_sorted_ids.html)- from_ - sorted_ - ids
- Encode a sorted list of doc ids as gaps (delta encoding).
- [gaps_](https://docs.rs/fn.gaps_from_sorted_ids_unchecked.html)- from_ - sorted_ - ids_ - unchecked
- Encode gaps without validating sort order.
- [ids_](https://docs.rs/fn.ids_from_gaps.html)- from_ - gaps
- Decode gaps back into absolute ids.
- [ids_](https://docs.rs/fn.ids_from_gaps_unchecked.html)- from_ - gaps_ - unchecked
- Decode gaps without overflow checking.

# PostingsIndex in postings - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/postings/0.2.0/postings/struct.PostingsIndex.html

## Expand description

A postings-based inverted index with segment-style updates.

This is an in-memory MVP:

- each `add_document`creates a new (small) segment
- deletes are logical (we update global stats; segment remains immutable)

## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/postings/lib.rs.html#345-366)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/postings/lib.rs.html#345-366)

Add a document by doc id and weighted term pairs.

Each `(term, weight)` pair represents a term and its weight in the document.
For classical indexing, weight is the term frequency (u32).
For learned sparse retrieval (SPLADE), weight is a continuous value (f32).

Duplicate terms are accumulated (weights summed).

If `doc_id` already exists, return an error. Call `delete_document` first
to model updates as delete+add (segment-style).

Term weight (frequency) of `term` in `doc_id`.

Returns `W::zero()` if the term is not present or the doc is unknown.
For classical indexes (`W = u32`), this is the term frequency count.
For learned sparse indexes (`W = f32`), this is the SPLADE weight.

Candidate documents that contain at least one query term.

Candidate documents that contain **all** query terms (conjunctive / AND).

This is a common first step before:

- exact phrase/proximity verification (positional index), or
- scoring (BM25/TF-IDF) in a higher layer.

Notes:

- Duplicate terms in `query_terms`are treated as a single requirement.
- Results are returned in sorted order.

#### pub fn [postings_iter](https://docs.rs#method.postings_iter)<'a, Q>(
    &'a self,

Iterate postings for a term across all segments (live docs only).

Reads from the global flat postings map in O(1) and filters out logically-deleted documents.

Return the top `k` documents by sparse inner product.

Query terms are borrowed so a `PostingsIndex<String, f32>` can be queried
with `&str` terms without allocating. Duplicate query terms are
accumulated before scoring. Ties are broken by ascending doc id.

# rustledger-validate 0.19.1 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/rustledger-validate/0.19.1

# rustledger-validate

Beancount validation with 26 error codes for ledger correctness.

## Error Categories

| Range | Category |
|---|---|
| E1xxx | Account errors (not opened, already closed, etc.) |
| E2xxx | Balance/pad errors |
| E3xxx | Transaction errors (unbalanced, no postings) |
| E4xxx | Inventory/lot errors |
| E5xxx | Currency/commodity-metadata errors |
| E7xxx | Option errors |
| E8xxx | Document errors |
| E10xxx | Date warnings |

## Example

Validation is run through a `ValidationSession`. Standalone callers
(LSP, FFI, tests on already-booked input) drive the two phases plus
`finalize` directly; the loader pipeline interleaves booking between
phases.

```
use ;
use ;
let directives:  = vec!;
let today = naive_date.unwrap;
let session = new;
let  = session.run_early;
let  = session.run_late;
errors.extend;
errors.extend;
for error in errors
```
The previous free-function shortcuts (`validate`, `validate_with_options`)
were removed in #1116 when validation was split around booking. Callers
must now thread state through a `ValidationSession` so that `Phase::Late`
sees the inventory state accumulated during `Phase::Early`.

## Features

- Parallel validation with rayon
- Configurable error severity
- Rich error messages with source locations

## License

GPL-3.0
